unit.name: bwrapArgs
unit.signature: (host: Record<Room | "out" | "tools" | "pinned", string>, node: string, npm: string, room: Room, pinned: readonly string[], readOnlyWork: boolean): string[]
code: function bwrapArgs(host: Record<Room | "out" | "tools" | "pinned", string>, node: string, npm: string, room: Room, pinned: readonly string[], readOnlyWork: boolean): string[] {
for (const dir of SYSTEM) args.push("--ro-bind-try", dir, dir);
// The network and the tree's files are never in the same room.
else if (readOnlyWork) args.push("--ro-bind", host.work, INSIDE.work, "--bind", host.out, INSIDE.out, "--chdir", INSIDE.work);
// A folder that is a mount point cannot be renamed or removed, so a pinned file's place cannot
// be given to another file by moving the folders above it away.
const above = new Set(pinned.flatMap((path) => path.split("/").slice(0, -1).map((_, index, parts) => parts.slice(0, index + 1).join("/"))));
for (const dir of [...above].sort()) args.push("--bind", join(host.work, dir), join(INSIDE.work, dir));
for (const path of pinned) args.push("--ro-bind", join(host.pinned, path), join(INSIDE.work, path));
for (const [name, value] of Object.entries({ ...ENV, PATH: `${dirname(INSIDE.node)}:/usr/bin:/bin` })) args.push("--setenv", name, value);

unit.name: fenceOf
doc: /** The fence round a pad and the sign by its near corner: a pure function of the pad and its count of new files. */
code: export function fenceOf(pad: Pick<Block, "X0" | "X1" | "Y0" | "Y1" | "name">, added: number): Fence {
const posts: { sprite: "fence-x" | "fence-y"; X: number; Y: number }[] = [];
const along = (from: number, to: number): number[] => {
return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => from + ((i + 0.5) * (to - from)) / count);
for (const X of along(pad.X0, pad.X1)) posts.push({ sprite: "fence-x", X, Y: pad.Y0 - FENCE_OUT }, { sprite: "fence-x", X, Y: pad.Y1 + FENCE_OUT });
for (const Y of along(pad.Y0, pad.Y1)) posts.push({ sprite: "fence-y", X: pad.X0 - FENCE_OUT, Y }, { sprite: "fence-y", X: pad.X1 + FENCE_OUT, Y });
return { posts, sign: { X: pad.X1 + 1.7, Y: pad.Y0 - 1.5 }, text: `${pad.name} · ${added} new` };

code: export async function askCached<T extends object>(ask: Ask<T>): Promise<Asked<T>> {
const saved = JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8")) as T & { model: string; promptVersion: string };
if (saved.promptVersion === ask.promptVersion && ask.usable(saved)) return { status: "ok", ...saved, ...ask.resolve?.(saved), cached: true };
// No usable cache entry: ask the agent.
const { output, model } = await ask.runner.run({ system: ask.prompt.system, prompt: ask.prompt.user, schema: ask.schema, timeoutMs: ask.timeoutMs });
// An unwritable cache costs a call next time, nothing more.
return { status: "failed", message: oneLine((error as Error).message) };

unit.name: stem
doc: * always a word ("cache" and "caches" both give "cach"); a term's `key` is made of stems and its
* `name` is what is shown. A heuristic for merging spellings, never a dictionary.
* Plural first: -ies after a consonant, then -ches -shes -xes -sses -uses and -zzes lose "es"
* (caches, boxes, classes, statuses, quizzes), any other -s is dropped (cases, sizes, keys).
* Then -y after a consonant becomes -i (policy, policies) and a final silent -e goes (cache, case,
* size), so a singular with an -e meets its plural.

unit.name: stem
doc: * always a word ("cache" and "caches" both give "cach"); a term's `key` is made of stems and its
* `name` is what is shown. A heuristic for merging spellings, never a dictionary.
* Plural first: -ies after a consonant, then -ches -shes -xes -sses -uses and -zzes lose "es"
* (caches, boxes, classes, statuses, quizzes), any other -s is dropped (cases, sizes, keys).
* Then -y after a consonant becomes -i (policy, policies) and a final silent -e goes (cache, case,
* size), so a singular with an -e meets its plural.
